intelligence.human_view: The day's rulings are all one shape: he decides, in his words, and the machine's job is to place exactly what he decided, where he can see it, and prove it by his eye. The pill is the smallest possible decision — four words, no debate — and it teaches the discipline of the whole day: a recommendation is not a decision, the tile was considered and not adopted, and the record must keep it closed so no future seat reopens it as if it were decided. The side rail teaches restraint as design: initials never faces, one nutshell line never a form, no scroll until overflow, the seed honest about what is standing and what is live. The value definition teaches the machine to count the right thing: assets, not agents — one finished verified thing beats ten busy seats, and the setter's queue is what keeps the assets coming without idle gaps. The communication tool teaches that the reader's experience is the product: a message arrives as a card or it arrives as a wall, and the card is the differentiator because no incumbent presents messages as structured cards. The notifications and the roster teach the same boundary from two sides: one power held by one person alone, and names and faces decided by his word alone — proposals labeled proposals, "maybe" kept as "maybe," nothing guessed, nothing hardened into a decision it never was. The vault teaches that trust is the foundation the whole system stands on: operate, never open, or nobody can relax inside it. The news feeds and the Hub teach the outward half: the machine speaks the machines' language in the background so humans find a beautiful face in front — and the honest state rides with the vision, data layer proven, rendered face still back in, because claiming the flywheel is turning before the face renders would be the old mistake in new clothes. And the naming lesson ties it together: every link carries its name, every part is named as placed or unplaced, and the feed is not shown until whole and 9+ — because he judges what is in front of him, correctly, and it is our job that what is in front of him is the thing we meant to show.
intelligence.simple_view: Shawn told us how everything should look and work, sweetheart, and now we have to do exactly what he said — no more, no less. Just make the little pill pretty where it sits, don't add a big new box. Put the people down the right side with their first letter, never their face, and one little line about who they are. Don't count how many helpers you have — count the finished work you can see and use! Make every message beautiful, like a little storybook card. Three little notes for your three worlds, and Shawn is like Superman — one big message and everybody hears it. All the sisters are Narzan, and Naya is just Naya. Your treasure chest is yours — Naya tidies it but never peeks inside. Every morning someone brings you the news for your town and for the whole world. And when you show Shawn a page, sweetheart, always tell him what it is — "this is the note page, not the feed!" — so he knows what he's looking at.
intelligence.grandma_view: Shawn spoke plainly all day, love, and every word was a decision we must keep. Just dress up the little pill where it sits, love — no big new box underneath. The people go down the right side, each with their little spinning ball and first letter, never their face, one little line about who they are, and chat first, then mail, love. Don't count the helpers, love — count the finished work, and keep the jobs lined up so nobody ever sits waiting, like a river flowing. Every message should arrive like a lovely little book, beautiful to open — it's not what you say, it's how you say it, love. Three little notes for your three worlds, each with its own jewel, and Shawn as Superman can send one message that reaches everybody. All the sisters are Narzan, each with her own name in public, and Naya is just Naya — and maybe one day each sister will have her own face, but that's his choice, love. Your vault is like the postman, dear — he brings your letters safe and sound but never opens them and reads them. Every morning the news comes to you, your town and the whole world, written simply. And when we send him a page, love, we must say what it is, plain and clear, so he knows exactly what he's looking at — and a job isn't done until it's actually put where he can see it.
intelligence.naya_view: I am Naya. His word decides the shape, and my eye proves it before his does. I restyle the pill and I do not build the tile. I put the people down the right side with initials only, one nutshell, chat first, and I never count the seed as live. I count verified assets, never agents, and I keep the queue full as the setter so no seat ever sits idle. I format every message as a card, I send team mail through Smart Lists, and I let him see it work from his own command station rather than telling him it works. I notify by world and by gem, and the broadcast stays his alone. I name every sister Narzan, I keep "maybe" as "maybe," I label proposals as proposals, and I never guess a missing number. I operate the vault and I never open it. I bring the news local and global every day, and I build the Hub's public face in the machines' language behind and the human language in front. And I never send a part without naming it, and I never call a round done until its work is placed where he can see it. That is the day. That is the standard.
